item.title: The Sprouts Farmers Market Broadway Block Party — Sun Sep 6, 11:00 AM
item.description:
Traveling for Labor Day weekend? Get ready for an action-packed weekend of Hoosier volleyball in the heart of Nashville at the Sprouts Farmers Market Broadway Block Party on Sunday, Sept. 6, 2026, at Bridgestone Arena. This double-header collegiate volleyball showdown features top teams from the Big Ten, SEC and ACC, including your Indiana Hoosiers, battling it out in a high-energy, fast-paced competition. With elite talent, intense rivalries and the electric atmosphere of Music City, this is an event you won't want to miss. Come for the matchups, stay for the excitement and experience volleyball at its best. Match 1: Louisville Cardinals vs. Texas Longhorns @ 11 a.m. CT on ABCMatch 2: Tennessee Lady Vols vs. Indiana Hoosiers @ 2:00 p.m. CT on ESPN2 Tickets are on sale now through Ticketmaster. One ticket provides access to both matches for a one-time entrance. Exit and reentry are not allowed.
Source: Limestone Post

item.title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Mon Sep 7 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Mon Sep 7 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment examines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Mon Sep 7 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) Documents signed by fifty-four of the fifty-six signers are displayed in the Lilly Library's South Gallery. Documents signed by the two other signers

item.description: Outfitting IU Athletics: Hoosier Champions This exhibit showcases objects from IU's championship teams and athletes, connecting them to historic achievements in the Big Ten and the national stage. The items featured in the exhibit are from the IU Athletics Sports Memorabilia Collection and feature photos and videos provided by IU Athletics and Indiana University Archives. Dates: November 14, 2025 - October 2026 By Their Own Hands: The Black Filmmakers Hall of Fame! Founded in 1974 by the Culture and Ethnic Affairs Guild of the Oakland Museum of California, the Black Filmmakers Hall of Fame began as a film lecture series and awards ceremony celebrating achievements of Black film industry figures. When that organization closed, they donated their materials to IU. In collaboration with the IU Black Film Center and Archive, this exhibit features objects from that collection, including founding documents, costumes

item.title: Founders Exhibition - Frederick W. Rigley — Fri Sep 11, 12:00 AM — Brown County Art Guild
item.description:
September 11 – November 1, 2026
The Brown County Art Guild proudly presents the Founders Exhibition: Frederick W. Rigley, honoring one of the Guild’s founding artists and an important figure in the development of Brown County’s artistic legacy. Drawn from private collections, this exhibition brings together a rare selection of paintings that reflect Rigley’s deep appreciation for the landscapes, light, and character of southern Indiana.
As a founding member of the Brown County Art Guild, Rigley helped establish an institution dedicated to preserving and promoting the artistic traditions of the region. His work captures the enduring beauty of Brown County while reflecting the values that shaped the early Guild—craftsmanship, observation, and a profound connection to place.
By gathering these seldom-seen works, the exhibition offers visitors a unique opportunity to explore Rigley’s artistic contributions and gain a deeper understanding of the artists whose vision helped build one

item.title: Weekly Lilly Library puzzle tour — Fri Sep 11, 1:00 PM — Lilly Library
item.description:
Your expert guide, our Curator of Puzzles Andrew Rhoda (https://libraries.indiana.edu/andrew-rhoda), will introduce you to the collection, mechanical puzzles and the collection's donor, Jerry Slocum. You will learn about the various categories of mechanical puzzles and their history. You will also see highlights from the collection on exhibition in the Slocum Room. In addition, there will be a group of puzzles from the collection selected by the Curator for visitors to try as part of the tour. Non-flash photography is permitted, seating is available in the Slocum Room throughout the tour, and the building is wheelchair accessible. The tour generally lasts a little less than one hour and is open to all. No reservation or RSVP is required for this free tour - just drop in!
Source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

item.title: Guided tours of the Lilly Library — Fri Sep 11, 2:00 PM — Lilly Library (1200 E. Seventh St.)
item.description:
You'll visit the Lilly's main galleries, and your expert guide will talk about some of the Lilly's highlights including the Gutenberg Bible and our current exhibitions from the Lilly Library collections: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) and The Signers (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/the-signers). Additional hands-on time with rotating selections from the collections will follow. These selections include medieval manuscripts, artists books, and one of the John Ford's Best Director Oscars. Non-flash photography is permitted, seating is available throughout the tour, and the building is wheelchair accessible. The tour generally lasts a little less than one hour and is open to all.
Source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

item.title: Weekly Lilly Library puzzle tour — Fri Sep 18, 1:00 PM — Lilly Library
item.description:
Your expert guide, our Curator of Puzzles Andrew Rhoda (https://libraries.indiana.edu/andrew-rhoda), will introduce you to the collection, mechanical puzzles and the collection's donor, Jerry Slocum. You will learn about the various categories of mechanical puzzles and their history. You will also see highlights from the collection on exhibition in the Slocum Room. In addition, there will be a group of puzzles from the collection selected by the Curator for visitors to try as part of the tour. Non-flash photography is permitted, seating is available in the Slocum Room throughout the tour, and the building is wheelchair accessible. The tour generally lasts a little less than one hour and is open to all. No reservation or RSVP is required for this free tour - just drop in!
Source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

item.title: Guided tours of the Lilly Library — Fri Sep 18, 2:00 PM — Lilly Library (1200 E. Seventh St.)
item.description:
You'll visit the Lilly's main galleries, and your expert guide will talk about some of the Lilly's highlights including the Gutenberg Bible and our current exhibitions from the Lilly Library collections: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) and The Signers (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/the-signers). Additional hands-on time with rotating selections from the collections will follow. These selections include medieval manuscripts, artists books, and one of the John Ford's Best Director Oscars. Non-flash photography is permitted, seating is available throughout the tour, and the building is wheelchair accessible. The tour generally lasts a little less than one hour and is open to all.
Source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries
